applies_why: The judge gives UNDERDETERMINED reasons based on the almah/bethulah word-count cutting both ways and chapter bounds, invoking ambiguity as a ground.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed whether 'cuts both ways' invokes a forbidden ambiguity ground versus merely noting lexical evidence.
why: The judge makes 'the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8)' a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, treating a two-way verse/word issue as open contrary to K-S2.
